chapter_guidelines.content:
The principles of multiple coding of injuries should be followed in coding 
fractures. Fractures of specified sites are coded individually by site in 
accordance with both the provisions within categories S02, S12, S22, S32, S42, 
S49, S52, S59, S62, S72, S79, S82, S89, S92 and the level of detail furnished by 
medical record content. 
 
A fracture not indicated as open or closed should be coded to closed. A fracture 
not indicated whether displaced or not displaced should be coded to displaced. 
 
More specific guidelines are as follows:

sections.content:
fractures 
Traumatic fractures are coded using the appropriate 7th character for 
initial encounter (A, B, C) for each encounter where the patient is 
receiving active treatment for the fracture. The appropriate 7th character 
for initial encounter should also be assigned for a patient who delayed 
seeking treatment for the fracture or nonunion. 
 
Fractures are coded using the appropriate 7th character for subsequent 
care for encounters after the patient has completed active treatment of the 
fracture and is receiving routine care for the fracture during the healing 
or recovery phase. 
 
Care for complications of surgical treatment for fracture repairs during 
the healing or recovery phase should be coded with the appropriate 
complication codes. 
 
Care of complications of fractures, such as malunion and nonunion, 
should be reported with the appropriate 7th character for subsequent care 
with nonunion (K, M, N,) or subsequent care with malunion (P, Q, R). 
 
Malunion/nonunion: The appropriate 7th character for initial encounter 
should also be assigned for a patient who delayed seeking treatment for 
the fracture or nonunion. 
 
The open fracture designations in the assignment of the 7th character for 
fractures of the forearm, femur and lower leg, including ankle are based 
on the Gustilo open fracture classification. When the Gustilo 
classification type is not specified for an open fracture, the 7th character 
for open fracture type I or II should be assigned (B, E, H, M, Q). 
 
A code from category M80, not a traumatic fracture code, should be used 
for any patient with known osteoporosis who suffers a fracture, even if 
the patient had a minor fall or trauma, if that fall or trauma would not 
usually break a normal, healthy bone. 
 
See Section I.C.13. Osteoporosis. 
 
The aftercare Z codes should not be used for aftercare for traumatic 
fractures. For aftercare of a traumatic fracture, assign the acute fracture 
code with the appropriate 7th character.
sections.title: Initial vs. subsequent encounter for fractures

sections.content:
Multiple fractures are sequenced in accordance with the severity of the 
fracture.
sections.title: Multiple fractures sequencing

sections.content:
For physeal fractures, assign only the code identifying the type of 
physeal fracture. Do not assign a separate code to identify the specific 
bone that is fractured.

- Same-day documentation describes a wrist fracture after a fall, but laterality conflicts across notes.
- ED note documents: "Patient with left wrist fracture after fall, splint applied."

gaps.text:
Laterality conflict for the fracture
- Why it matters: ICD-10-CM forearm/radius fracture coding requires side specificity when documented; conflicting side documentation creates coding and patient-safety risk.
- Evidence quotes:
  - "Patient with left wrist fracture after fall, splint applied."
  - "Right wrist fracture, cast applied."
  - "Patient reports pain on right wrist."
- Minimal clarification needed: Confirm the correct side of the wrist/distal radius fracture.

Fracture site terminology is not aligned across notes
- Why it matters: The radiology report specifies "distal radius," while clinical notes say only "wrist fracture." The most accurate diagnosis documentation should identify the actual bone/site when known.
- Evidence quotes:
  - "Left wrist fracture"
  - "Right wrist fracture"
  - "Linear fracture distal radius, side not specified."
- Minimal clarification needed: Clarify whether the injury should be documented as a distal radius fracture rath

Fracture pattern remains nonspecific
- Why it matters: Category S52.5 has more specific fracture options for lower end of radius; current wording supports at minimum a lower-end/distal radius fracture, but not a more specific pattern.
- Evidence quotes:
  - "Linear fracture distal radius, side not specified."
- Minimal clarification needed: If known and clinically documented, specify the fracture type/pattern of the distal radius; if not known, document as unspecified distal radius fracture.

Open vs closed status is not documented
- Why it matters: Traumatic fracture coding requires encounter/fracture detail; if open/closed is not documented, coding defaults to closed, but explicit documentation is preferable. Coding guidance indicates a fracture not indicated as open or closed is coded to closed.
- Evidence quotes:
  - "left wrist fracture after fall, splint applied."
  - "Right wrist fracture, cast applied."
  - "Linear fracture distal radius"
- Minimal clarification needed: State

text:
Encounter Summary:
- Same-day documentation describes a wrist fracture after a fall, but laterality conflicts across notes.
- ED note documents: "Patient with left wrist fracture after fall, splint applied."
- Orthopedic note documents: "Right wrist fracture, cast applied."
- Radiology documents: "Linear fracture distal radius, side not specified."
- Patient-reported symptom supports the right side: "Patient reports pain on right wrist."

Documentation Gaps:
1. Laterality conflict for the fracture
- Why it matters: ICD-10-CM forearm/radius fracture coding requires side specificity when documented; conflicting side documentation creates coding and patient-safety risk.
- Evidence quotes:
  - "Patient with left wrist fracture after fall, splint applied."
  - "Right wrist fracture, cast applied."
  - "Patient reports pain on right wrist."
- Minimal clarification needed: Confirm the correct side of the wrist/distal radius fracture.

2. Fracture site terminology is not aligned across notes
- Why it matters: The radiology report specifies "distal radius," while clinical notes say only "wrist fracture." The most accurate diagnosis documentation should identify the actual bone/site when known.
- Evidence quotes:
  - "Left wrist fracture"
  - "Right wrist fracture"
  - "Linear fracture distal radius, side not specified."
- Minimal clarification needed: Clarify whether the injury should be documented as a distal radius fracture rather than a nonspecific wrist fracture, and indicate the correct side.

3. Fracture pattern remains nonspecific
- Why it matters: Category S52.5 has more specific fracture options for lower end of radius; current wording supports at minimum a lower-end/distal radius fracture, but not a more specific pattern.
- Evidence quotes:
  - "Linear fracture distal radius, side not specified."
- Minimal clarification needed: If known and clinically documented, specify the fracture type/pattern of the distal radius; if not known, document as unspecified distal radius fracture.

4. Open vs closed status is not documented
- Why it matters: Traumatic fracture coding requires encounter/fracture detail; if open/closed is not documented, coding defaults to closed, but explicit documentation is preferable. Coding guidance indicates a fracture not indicated as open or closed is coded to closed.
- Evidence quotes:
  - "left wrist fracture after fall, splint applied."
  - "Right wrist fracture, cast applied."
  - "Linear fracture distal radius"
- Minimal clarification needed: State whether the fracture was open or closed, if known.

Proposed Provider Queries:
1. Topic: Fracture laterality and anatomic site clarification
- Reason query is needed: Same-day records conflict on side, and radiology identifies distal radius without side.
- Evidence quote:
  - "Patient with left wrist fracture after fall, splint applied."
  - "Right wrist fracture, cast applied."
  - "Linear fracture distal radius, side not specified."
  - "Patient reports pain on right wrist."
- Non-leading query text:
  - "The record contains conflicting documentation regarding the wrist fracture laterality. ED documentation states 'left wrist fracture,' the orthopedic note states 'right wrist fracture,' and radiology describes a 'linear fracture distal radius' without side. Based on your clinical assessment and the available imaging, please clarify the correct anatomic site and laterality of the fracture for this encounter."
- Suggested response options:
  - Right distal radius fracture
  - Left distal radius fracture
  - Right wrist fracture, site not further specified
  - Left wrist fracture, site not further specified
  - Other, please specify
  - Clinically undetermined / unable to determine

2. Topic: Distal radius fracture specificity
- Reason query is needed: Radiology supports distal radius involvement, but current documentation does not clearly reconcile this with the final diagnosis terminology.
- Evidence quote:
  - "Linear fracture distal radius, side not specified."
  - "Right wrist fracture, cast applied."
- Non-leading query text:
  - "Radiology documents a 'linear fracture distal radius,' while clinical documentation describes a wrist fracture. If known, please clarify the fracture diagnosis for this encounter with the most specific anatomic description supported by the clinical record."
- Suggested response options:
  - Distal/lower end radius fracture
  - Wrist fracture, not further specified
  - Other fracture diagnosis, please specify
  - Clinically undetermined / unable to determine

3. Topic: Open vs closed fracture status
- Reason query is needed: Fracture status is not explicitly stated.
- Evidence quote:
  - "left wrist fracture after fall, splint applied."
  - "Right wrist fracture, cast applied."
- Non-leading query text:
  - "For the documented wrist/distal radius fracture, if known, please clarify whether the fracture was open or closed at the time of this encounter."
- Suggested response options:
  - Closed fracture
  - Open fracture
  - Other, please specify
  - Clinically undetermined / unable to determine

Coding Specificity Checklist:
- Correct laterality: right vs left
- Exact anatomic site: wrist vs distal/lower end of radius
- Fracture pattern/type, if known and documented
- Open vs closed status
- Encounter status for fracture care when relevant to code selection
- Any additional associated forearm/wrist fracture details if present elsewhere in the chart

Risk Flags:
- Direct contradiction in laterality: ED says left; orthopedic note says right.
- Radiology does not specify side, so imaging does not independently resolve the contradiction.
- Symptom documentation ("pain on right wrist") supports but does not by itself definitively override the conflicting ED diagnosis.
- Splint in ED and cast in ortho may reflect progression of treatment, but they do not resolve the side discrepancy.

Specialist Trace:
- Medical Coding Expert consulted: Yes.
- Requested: Review coding/CDI specificity issues for laterality conflict, fracture site specificity, and contradictions.
- Accepted from expert:
  - Distal/lower end of radius falls under ICD-10-CM S52.5 family, which has more specific options than nonspecific forearm fracture.
  - Laterality matters for code assignment; examples returned included right lower-end radius vs unspecified radius codes.
  - Coding guideline accepted: when open/closed is not documented, coding defaults to closed.
- Rejected/limited:
  - No patient-specific code assignment was adopted because the chart contains unresolved laterality conflict and insufficient fracture-pattern detail.
- AMBOSS Expert consulted: No; not required because no clinical diagnostic criteria question needed resolution.
- CDI Web Search Expert consulted: No; existing coding expert output provided sufficient coding guidance for this excerpt.

Most constrained coding takeaway:
- Do not finalize a side-specific diagnosis code until the provider resolves the laterality conflict.
- If unresolved, the record supports only an unspecified distal/lower-end radius fracture concept more safely than a side-specific assignment, but provider clarification is preferred before coding.
